title: 3. Distribution, Supply Chain & Unit Economics

epigraph.quote: In heavy minerals, geology decides your raw material cost, but logistics decides your addressable market.
epigraph.author: Industrial Supply-Chain Rule

web_blocks.html: Geography and process engineering anchor RPEL's supply chain. Its main plants in Kaladera (Jaipur) and Newai (Tonk, Rajasthan) sit right beside India's purest crystalline quartz deposits (97.5%–99.5%+ SiO2) [2][19]. Inside the automated Newai lines—including wholly owned subsidiary Raghav Productivity Solutions Private Limited (RPSPL)—raw quartz lumps go through multi-stage crushing, vertical shaft impactor (VSI) shaping, and high-intensity magnetic separation [2][24]. Automated optical sorting and computerized silo blending then lock in batch consistency [2][24]. Technical advisor Jan W. Kjellberg (JWK AB Sweden, former president of Svenska Silica) helped RPEL's engineers refine granulometry curves and foundry protocols [24].

Because silica ramming mass is dense and bulky, freight cost per tonne limits a single plant's economic radius. Shipping bagged ramming mass from Rajasthan to steel belts in Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal added heavy road freight [8][9]. That cost left Eastern India open to regional rivals [8][9]. RPEL's September 2026 joint venture with TRL Krosaki Refractories Ltd builds a 350,000 MTPA plant in Odisha with captive access to TRL Krosaki's quartzite mines [6][8]. That plant removes the freight penalty and opens a coastal export route through eastern ports [6][8].

web_blocks.html: The FY26 unit-economics waterfall shows both strong operating margins and a clear working-capital drag [1]. Keeping operating expenses at 70.8% of revenue alongside tiny interest costs (₹1 Cr) sends 21.4% of every revenue rupee straight to net profit [1]. Yet working capital absorbed ₹18 Cr between PAT (₹55 Cr) and CFO (₹37 Cr) [1]. Specifically, Inventory Days climbed from 223 days in FY25 to 272 days in FY26, up from 159 days in FY23 [1].

On collections, RPEL's distribution discipline improved sharply. Debtor Days fell from 131 days in FY22 and 109 days in FY24 to 83 days in FY26, even as sales nearly doubled over those two years [1]. Days Payable held steady at 100 days in FY26, partly offsetting the inventory build [1]. As exports approach half of standalone revenue, longer container transit times and strategic quartz-lump stocking explain part of those 272 inventory days [1][22]. Still, normalizing inventory turns will be vital to lift CFO/EBITDA back above 85% [1][22].

web_blocks.title: Forensic Working-Capital Tension: 272 Inventory Days vs. 83 Debtor Days
paragraphs: RPEL's Debtor Days improved steadily from 131 days (FY22) to 83 days (FY26), proving tighter credit control over secondary steel buyers [1]. By contrast, Inventory Days rose to 272 days and the Cash Conversion Cycle stretched to 255 days in FY26 [1]. Stocking high-purity quartz lumps and export containers buffers supply shocks, yet investors must check whether 270+ inventory days reflect strategic mineral buffers or slower-moving grades [1].

book_paragraphs: To understand RPEL's unit economics, you and I have to follow a chunk of quartz from the Rajasthan hillside all the way into a container bound for Dubai or a truck heading to Raipur. At the front end of the supply chain, RPEL enjoys a geological gift: its Kaladera and Newai plants sit right on top of Rajasthan's high-purity quartz reserves. Inside the automated Newai lines, quartz lumps are crushed, shaped in vertical shaft impactors, passed through high-intensity magnetic separators to yank out iron impurities, and sorted into sealed silos. Under the technical guidance of Jan W. Kjellberg of Sweden's JWK AB, the company turned what used to be a dusty quarry operation into a precision blending plant.

Now look at the other end of the supply chain: freight. Ramming mass is heavy. You cannot haul bagged silica across 1,500 kilometers of Indian highways to Jharkhand or Odisha without freight eating a chunk of your margin. That is why the September 2026 Odisha joint venture with TRL Krosaki is such a smart supply-chain move. By placing a 350,000-tonne plant right next to TRL Krosaki's Odisha quartzite mines and Eastern India's induction furnace belt, RPEL cuts domestic haulage distances and gains direct access to eastern ports.

book_subsections.title: Walking the ₹100 Revenue Waterfall
paragraphs: When you and I break down every ₹100 of FY26 revenue—₹257 crore in total—the P&L looks remarkably clean. Roughly ₹70.82 goes to raw materials, power, payroll, and plant overhead, leaving ₹29.18 in operating EBITDA. Depreciation takes ₹2.72, interest takes a negligible ₹0.39, other income adds ₹0.78, and taxes take roughly ₹5.84, leaving ₹21.40 as pure net profit. Very few industrial mineral businesses convert more than a fifth of their top line into bottom-line profit.

Yet the cash-flow bridge tells a more nuanced story that we should not gloss over. Out of that ₹21.40 in net profit per ₹100 of sales, only ₹14.40 arrived as operating cash flow in FY26, and ₹8.95 remained as free cash flow after ₹5.45 of capex. Where did the gap go? Straight into the yard. Inventory days climbed from 159 days in FY23 to 260 in FY24, dipped to 223 in FY25, and hit 272 days in FY26, pushing the cash conversion cycle to 255 days.

The encouraging offset is that debtor days actually fell from 131 days in FY22 to 83 days in FY26—meaning customers are paying faster, not slower, even as revenue nearly doubled from ₹133 crore to ₹257 crore. Still, holding nearly nine months of inventory is a working-capital habit we will watch closely.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: A 29% EBITDA margin proves customers value the product, but 272 inventory days remind us that high-purity mineral supply chains tie up real cash in raw-material yards.
